id.description: Action id, unique in the definition

fields.description: Cell values keyed by field name or id. Fields the caller cannot read are absent.

parent_id.description: Parent record (sub-records, SPEC §5.7): same as writing the `parent` field; `null` makes the record a root. Not together with the `parent` field itself. A table without a `parent` field the caller reads answers `422 VALIDATION_FAILED` (`SUBRECORDS_NOT_ENABLED`).

fields.description: Cell values keyed by field name or id. Fields the caller cannot read are absent.

parent_id.description: Parent record (sub-records, SPEC §5.7): same as writing the `parent` field; `null` makes the record a root. Not together with the `parent` field itself. A table without a `parent` field the caller reads answers `422 VALIDATION_FAILED` (`SUBRECORDS_NOT_ENABLED`).

generate.description: `webhook_signing` only, instead of `value`: the server generates a `whsec_` secret of 32 bytes and returns it **once** in `value` of the response

name.description: Shown to automation managers (unique in the organization)

value.description: Write-only: a bot token (`123456:ABC…`), a header value (printable ASCII) or a `whsec_…` signing secret (24–64 bytes). Never returned; send a new one to replace it

password.description: Stored as an argon2id hash; never returned

filename.description: Original file name (kept in `meta.attachments`, never in keys)

mime.description: MIME type (`type/subtype`, parameters ignored); must match the field’s `accept`

size.description: Exact size in bytes; the upload URL is signed for it

config.description: Settings by view type (`ViewConfig`): grid → common keys; kanban → also `kanban`; form → also `form`. Validated against the table and the saver’s field permissions.

layout.description: Default: 6 × 6 at column 0 below every widget

version.description: Expected dashboard `version` (same as `If-Match`); a mismatch is `409`

last_used_at.description: Written at most once per 5 minutes

token.description: The token (`cht_…`, 40 characters): returned only in this response (and in its replay for the same `Idempotency-Key`, whose stored copy is encrypted) — never logged or stored in clear

email_sent.description: Whether an email is being sent (SMTP configured)

invite_url.description: One-time link `<PUBLIC_URL>/invite/<token>`; returned only in this response (and in its replay for the same `Idempotency-Key`, whose stored copy is encrypted), never logged

table_id.description: Table of the view or form; `null` for a dashboard link

target_name.description: Name of the target view, form or dashboard; `null` when it no longer exists

token.description: 32 random bytes, base64url; returned only once

version.description: Bumped by every change of the dashboard, its layout or its widgets; send it back (`If-Match` or `version`) to avoid lost updates

targets.description: One field per table; the field must fit `kind`

DashboardList.description: The dashboards the caller can see, by position

DateReachedTrigger.description: Fires once per (record, value) when the date of `field_id` plus `offset_minutes` passes after the automation was turned on; a new value fires again. `field_id`: `datetime`, `created_at` or a stored formula/lookup of a date type (virtual → `INVALID_FIELD_TYPE`). Date-only values fire at `time_of_day` (default 09:00) in the field’s time zone. Trashed records and records `run_as` cannot read never fire. Run data: `due_at`

offset_minutes.description: Minutes after (positive) or before (negative) the date

time_of_day.description: Date-only fields: time of day in the field’s zone (default 09:00)

DateReminderOption.description: `options.reminder` of a `datetime` field (`null` = off; CONTRACTS §22.6). When a record’s date plus `offset_minutes` passes (date-only values at `time_of_day`, default 09:00, in the field’s time zone, else the organization’s), a `date.reminder` notification goes to the users of `user_field_id` at that moment or to `user_ids`; each recipient must read the record and the date field (and, with `field_user`, the recipient field) when it is sent. Turning it on or changing it never reminds of moments already passed. Saving it needs the right to change the schema.

offset_minutes.description: Minutes after (positive) or before (negative) the date, −43200 … 43200

time_of_day.description: Date-only fields only: time of day in the field’s zone (`null` = 09:00); must be `null` on a field with a time

user_field_id.description: A `user` or `created_by` field of the same table, read when the reminder fires

offset_minutes.description: Minutes after (positive) or before (negative) the date, −43200 … 43200

time_of_day.description: Date-only fields only: time of day in the field’s zone (`null` = 09:00); must be `null` on a field with a time

minutes.description: Wait this long (1 minute – 30 days); `null` when `until` is set

recheck_condition.description: Filter on the trigger record, re-evaluated when the delay ends

until.description: Wait until this date (`YYYY-MM-DD` = midnight, `YYYY-MM-DDTHH:mm` in the organization zone, or an ISO instant), e.g. `{ "field": "fld_due" }`; at most 30 days ahead (else the step fails `invalid_value`), already past = no wait

id.description: Action id, unique in the definition

dependents.description: Field: views and roles using it (like `convert-preview`) and the formula/lookup fields that would be `REF`; table: the formula/lookup fields of other tables that would be `REF`. Only what the caller can see

DeleteRecordAction.description: Moves the trigger record to the trash

id.description: Action id, unique in the definition

children.description: `promote` (default): children of deleted records become roots. `delete`: descendants the caller may delete go to the trash too (same request, same `batch_id`); a descendant the caller cannot delete becomes a root with its own branch.

name.description: Default: the source name followed by ` (copy)` / ` (bản sao)` in the language of the caller, the source name cut so the whole name stays within 255 characters
Default: the source name followed by ` (copy)` / ` (bản sao)` in the caller’s language (then ` 2`, ` 3`… while taken)
Default: the source name followed by ` copy` (then ` copy 2`, …)

EffectiveAccess.description: What the caller may do in the base (CONTRACTS §5A). Lists only what the caller can see.

markdown.description: What to insert in the Markdown: `![name](asset:att_… =width)` (`]` and `\` of the name escaped as `\]`, `\\`)

url.description: Where the editor previews it (`302` to a signed URL valid 60 s, for the same people who may upload it)

size.description: Exact size in bytes (at most 10485760); the upload URL is signed for it

display_name_issue.description: `null`, or why the stored display name would be refused today (saved before the rule; kept and still used until changed)

EmailIdentitySmtp.description: SMTP server of the identity (never the password)

host.description: Host name or IP address of the SMTP server (no scheme, no port)

url.description: Signed URL valid 60 s, for the person previewing only (never sent): replace `cid:` sources with it to show the image in the sandboxed preview

EmailRecipientLiteral.description: One address or a list of addresses

EmailSettings.description: Instance SMTP status, email limits and automation email settings of the organization (never the SMTP password or full URL)

max_attachment_bytes.description: Env `EMAIL_MAX_ATTACHMENT_BYTES`: cap of the organization value

max_attachments.description: Env `EMAIL_MAX_ATTACHMENTS`: cap of the organization value

max_inline_images.description: Env `EMAIL_MAX_INLINE_IMAGES`: images of one automation email, signature included (T534); their bytes count toward `max_attachment_bytes`

EmailTestResult.description: Outcome of the SMTP connection test

ai_state.description: Only on AI fields (`options.ai`, T910): counts of rows waiting, failed and paused

button.description: Only on `button` fields returned by the field endpoints (T517): the automation attached to the button and its `min_permission`

automation_id.description: The automation (not deleted) attached to the button; `null` = none

min_permission.description: Least permission on a record to click (`null` without automation)

compute_error.description: Only on `formula`/`lookup` fields: `null`, or the field-level error

refs.description: What the error is about (`REF`: the missing field/table, or the computed field in error it reads; `CIRCLE`: the fields of the cycle; `INVALID_CONFIG`: the converted field, when known). `id`/`name` are `null` for what the reader cannot see: a field or table without read access, a field in the trash without schema rights on its table, a table in the trash for non-admins, anything purged

compute_mode.description: Only on `formula`/`lookup` fields, chosen by the server (SPEC §5.9): `stored` (a column, computed on write) or `virtual` (computed on read: `NOW()`/`TODAY()` or a virtual dependency)

compute_state.description: Only on `formula`/`lookup` fields: `ready`, `backfilling` (values being computed for every record), `recomputing` (a write changed more than 1 000 rows of it, or every row: the `computed.recompute` job catches up and rows not recomputed yet keep their previous values) or `error` (see `compute_error`)

deleted_at.description: Only on fields in the trash, listed with `include_deleted=true`: when the field was deleted (restorable for 30 days)

link_table_purged.description: Only on `link` fields in the trash (listed with `include_deleted=true`) whose linked table was purged (`true`, T461): the links are gone and a restore answers `422 VALIDATION_FAILED` / `LINK_TABLE_PURGED` (CONTRACTS §13)

link_target_deleted.description: Only on `link` fields whose linked table is in the trash (`true`): the field stays, its cells read empty and take no new links until the table is restored (CONTRACTS §13)

locked.description: Only on `formula`/`lookup` fields (T457): `true` when the reader cannot read what the value is computed from — another table, a field of other records, or (base setting `strict_computed_permissions`) a field of the same record it cannot read. Its cells read `null`; filtering, sorting and grouping by it answer like a hidden field (`422 INVALID_FILTER` / `INVALID_SORT`). Also on AI fields (T910, always strict): `true` when the reader cannot read every field of its prompt

position.description: Sort key of the display order

result_type.description: Only on `formula`/`lookup` fields: the type of their value (T456)

to.description: Value after the conversion (`null` when lost; for `invalid`, unchanged)

link_change.description: Link conversions (T404; the type stays `link`). While `running`, record writes to the field go on (the junction keeps its structure); only schema changes are locked

status.description: `running`: values are being converted; the field shows its old definition and values, read-only (schema changes of it and record writes to it answer `409 SCHEMA_LOCKED`). `succeeded`: converted, revertible until `revertible_until`

FieldDependent.description: Something that uses the field and may stop working after the change: a view (filter, sort, group, kanban, form), a role (field rule, record filter; base admins only), a formula/lookup field that would get a field-level error (`REF`, or `INVALID_CONFIG` for a conversion; directly or through another computed field; only fields the caller can read are listed, T460) or an automation (once those exist)

name.description: Only for `type = field`: the name of the formula/lookup field

table_id.description: Only for `type = field`: the table of the formula/lookup field

FieldOptions.description: Options of the field type (SPEC §5.5), e.g. `style`, `default_value`; for `select`: `multiple` and `options` (`[{ id, name, color }]`). Validated per type (CONTRACTS §13); the options of `link`, `parent`, `formula` and `lookup` are described by the components `LinkFieldOptions`, `ParentFieldOptions`, `FormulaFieldOptions` and `LookupFieldOptions`; the `reminder` of a `datetime` field by `DateReminderOption`.

fields.description: Fields to return (`[]` = the primary field only)

id.description: Action id, unique in the definition

size.description: Exact size in bytes; the upload URL is signed for it

next_allowed_at.description: When the next period starts (`reached` only); `null` for `once` or when not reached

reached.description: Submitting now would be `409 SUBMISSION_LIMIT_REACHED`; always `false` for `none`

fields.description: Values keyed by field id; only fields of the form. Always typecast with the base locale (CONTRACTS §2), so values from URL prefill (`?prefill_<field_id>=…`) can be sent as strings; select options are never created. Hidden prefilled fields are sent here too and validated like the others.

honeypot.description: Must be empty or absent: the value of a field hidden from people. A non-empty value gets the normal success response and nothing is written.

submit_token.description: From `GET /shares/{token}/submit-token`; required on the link route, ignored on the member route. Single use; at least the minimum fill time old.

redirect_url.description: Absolute `http(s)` URL to open after the submission, or `null`

success_message.description: Message to show; may be empty

not_before.description: Submitting with the token earlier is `SUBMITTED_TOO_FAST`

expression.description: The formula as written (SPEC §9.2): field and table **names** in `[…]`, stored with their IDs so renames never break it. Responses render the current names; a reference that no longer exists shows as `#REF[fld_…]`. Only given to readers with schema rights on the table who can read every table and field it references

style.description: Format of the result: a `number` style (`plain`, `currency`, …) for number results, `{ "format" }` of `datetime` fields for dates, `null` for anything else. Omitted on create: the style of the field the result carries (`[Số tiền] * 0.1` keeps a currency)

request_id.description: The stored request (`whr_…`). A replayed `webhook-id` gets the id of the duplicate entry of the log: no new event

private_addresses.description: `HTTP_PRIVATE_ALLOWLIST` of the instance: `off` — entries never open private addresses, they only allow another port on a public host

HttpAllowlistEntry.description: Host automations may call on a private network

created_by.description: `null` when that member left or the account is gone

host.description: The exact host, or the suffix of a wildcard

body.description: JSON value, text, or `null` for an empty body

HttpRequestAction.description: Output once delivered: `{ delivery_id, status, headers: { content-type }, body, body_truncated }` (`HttpStepOutput`; usable later as `{ "step": "act_…", "path": "body.id" }`); while waiting `{ delivery_id }`

id.description: Action id, unique in the definition

header_name.description: Header that carries the secret value (`Authorization`, `X-Api-Key`…)

secret_id.description: An `http_header` secret of the organization whose scope includes the base

body.description: Not with `GET`. A `Content-Type` header replaces the default type

fail_on_http_error.description: `false`: a final `3xx`/`4xx`/`5xx` ends the step `succeeded` with its `status` in the output (temporary statuses are still retried first)

headers.description: Header values are one line (line breaks become spaces), cut at 8,192 characters; names the outbox sets or that belong to the connection are `HEADER_NOT_ALLOWED`, like a name given twice

query.description: Parameters appended to the query of the URL (encoded)

signing_secret_id.description: A `webhook_signing` secret: the request carries `webhook-signature` (Standard Webhooks; two signatures for 24 hours after the secret is replaced)

url.description: The URL (`http`/`https`, ≤ 2,048 characters with the query); a literal is checked when saved (`INVALID_URL`), the address when called (CONTRACTS §25.4)

HttpRequestFormBody.description: `application/x-www-form-urlencoded`, one pair per field (values as text)

HttpRequestJsonBody.description: `application/json`: a literal is sent as its JSON; a template is rendered with each placeholder value escaped as JSON string content (write `"{{ [fld_…] }}"` for a string) and must then parse as JSON (`invalid_value`); a field, step or trigger value is sent as its JSON

HttpRequestValue.description: A value of SPEC §11.4 other than `digest`. Rendered as text: a template as text (in the URL each placeholder value is percent-encoded), a JSON string as is, any other JSON value as JSON text, `null` as ""

warnings.description: `no_sample`: `webhook.received` trigger without a captured sample — the request values were empty (T616)

draft.description: The builder's unsaved configuration of the step (default: the saved one): an `HttpRequestConfig` (has `method`) or a `RunN8nWorkflowConfig`, of the type of the saved step when it exists (another type → `404`)

record_id.description: A record of the trigger table the caller reads (`null` = no record); through an API token it also needs `records:read`

on_false.description: `stop` ends the run as `succeeded` when the conditions do not hold

id.description: Action id, unique in the definition
Global filter id or widget id, as sent

reason.description: `other_table`: it filters another table; `not_bound`: the widget does not follow this control (`filter_bindings`; for options: not a parent control); `self`: a cross-filter of the widget itself; `no_permission`: its field is one the viewer cannot read; `broken`: its field was deleted or no longer fits it

IncomingWebhook.description: An incoming webhook of a base

last_received_at.description: When the newest request still stored arrived (kept 7 days, replays included); `null` without one (T616)

listen_until.description: End of the "listen for a sample request" window, if open

signing_secret_rotating_until.description: Until then the previous signing secret is accepted too (24 h after a rotation)

url.description: `PUBLIC_URL/api/v1/hooks/<token>` (base admins only, like every field here)

usages.description: Automations (not deleted) triggered by this hook, by name

IncomingWebhookAuth.description: `signature`: Standard Webhooks signature (CONTRACTS §10); `bearer`: `Authorization: Bearer <token>`; `both`: both checks; `none`: anyone with the URL

listen_until.description: The first valid request before this time becomes the sample (180 s)

causation_accepted.description: A valid `X-Cellhive-Causation` header continued a chain

duplicate.description: Same `webhook-id` as an earlier request: accepted, no event

next_cursor.description: Cursor for the next page, `null` on the last page

listen_until.description: End of the open window; `null` when not listening

body.description: The body: JSON value, form fields as an object (repeated keys as arrays), `null` when empty; when `truncated`, the first 64 KB of the body as a string

query.description: Query string; repeated keys as arrays

name.description: `null` when the caller cannot see that automation

last_received_at.description: When the newest request still stored arrived (kept 7 days, replays included); `null` without one (T616)

listen_until.description: End of the "listen for a sample request" window, if open

signing_secret_rotating_until.description: Until then the previous signing secret is accepted too (24 h after a rotation)

url.description: `PUBLIC_URL/api/v1/hooks/<token>` (base admins only, like every field here)

usages.description: Automations (not deleted) triggered by this hook, by name

account_exists.description: True when an account with this email exists: sign in as that user to accept. Otherwise accept with `display_name` and `password`.

result.description: Outcome of a succeeded job, e.g. `{ "download_url", "expires_at", "size" }` for exports

fields.description: Values (`cell_format=json`) of the display fields, keyed by field id

full.description: Two-way link: the reverse cell of this record already holds its most links, so linking it fails with `TOO_MANY_VALUES`

selectable.description: Matches the record_filter of the field (always `true` without `ids`)

title.description: Primary field as text; `null` when the caller cannot read the primary field

count.description: Linked records now in the cell

limit.description: Most links of the cell (500, or 1)

fields.description: Display fields: the first non-primary fields of the linked table the caller reads

ids.description: Only these records, in this order ("selected only", recent picks): `record_filter` is not applied but reported as `selectable`; ids the caller cannot read are absent

record_id.description: The record whose cell is being edited: marks `linked` items and fills `cell` (a record the caller cannot read is `404`)

search.description: Unaccented, case-insensitive substring of the primary field of the linked table

allow_multiple.description: Default `true`; `false` keeps at most one linked record per cell

bidirectional.description: Default `false`. `true` creates the reverse field in the linked table (same junction); set on create only (changing it is a conversion, ADR-28)

bidirectional_link_field_name.description: Name of the reverse field of a two-way link (default: this table name)

record_filter.description: Filter DSL over fields of the linked table the saver can read; new links must match it

symmetric_field_id.description: Read-only: the reverse field of a two-way link (a written value is ignored)

links.description: Links its reverse cell would hold (> 500)

record_id.description: A record of the linked table

from.description: Source table (same base, readable by the saver)

select.description: Field of the source table whose values are taken

style.description: Format of the result: a `number` style (`plain`, `currency`, …) for number results, `{ "format" }` of `datetime` fields for dates, `null` for anything else. Omitted on create: the style of the field the result carries (`[Số tiền] * 0.1` keeps a currency)

where.description: Filter DSL (SPEC §6.1) on source fields, lookup mode: `intersects`/`disjoint` and `{ "field_ref": "<field of this table>" | "__id" }` values; at least one condition. `{ "field": "__id", "operator": "is_any_of" | "is_none_of", "value": { "field_ref": "<link field of this table to from>" } }`: the source record is (not) one of the records this record links to (one-way links included)

allow_writes.description: Off (default): tools that write are never listed nor callable, whatever the token scopes. On: listed for tokens with `records:write`

enabled.description: Off (default): `POST /api/v1/mcp` answers `403 MCP_DISABLED` before any JSON-RPC. On: members bring the data they can read to the LLM of the MCP client they choose

method.description: `server/discover`, `tools/list`, `tools/call` (2026-07-28, `_meta` envelope on every request); `initialize` and `notifications/initialized` for 2025-era clients

error.description: `-32602`: unknown or unlisted tool, bad params; `-32022`: unsupported protocol version; `-32020`: `Mcp-*` headers do not match the body

Me.description: The signed-in user and their organizations

locale.description: The user's locale, else their first organization's, else DEFAULT_LOCALE

timezone.description: The user's time zone, else their first organization's, else DEFAULT_TIMEZONE

email.description: Email the provider reported last (display only; never used to sign in)

last_login_at.description: Last sign-in through this identity; `null` when never used to sign in

provider_name.description: Button label of the provider (`OIDC_<SLUG>_NAME`); the slug when the provider is no longer configured

role.description: The caller's role in the organization

access.description: Exactly the `access` the member gets from `GET /bases/:id`; `null` when the member cannot open the base (`source.kind = none`)

counts.description: With `counts=true` and access: the first 20 visible tables (table order), counted with the member’s permissions; else `null`

revoke_tokens.description: Also revoke every API token of the user, in every organization (default `true`; `false` keeps them working)

N8nWorkflowPayload.description: JSON body of a `run_n8n_workflow` request (SPEC §13.3), built as `run_as` when the step runs: `record.fields` by field name (`cell_format=text`), `record.fields_by_id` by field id (`cell_format=json`), only fields `run_as` reads (linked records it cannot read have `title: null`); `record: null` without a trigger record or when `run_as` cannot read it; `table: null` without a trigger table; `changes` (`record.updated` with `include_changes`) by field name, in the `[@previous]` form. Never a secret or a token

data.description: Stored parameters of the type (CONTRACTS §22.1). `automation.batch_overflow` also has `skipped` (records of the batch the automation left out, or `null` when the caller cannot see the automation any more), computed when read, never stored. `record.assigned` and `record.followed_changed` gathered from the writes of an incoming webhook (one per hook, table and minute) have `source.incoming_webhook_id`; `record.followed_changed` then also has `record_ids` (at most 20) and `record_count`.

step.description: Action id, unique in the definition

next_cursor.description: Cursor for the next page, `null` on the last page

channel.description: `telegram` is listed only while the organization has a notification bot (CONTRACTS §22.7); a stored Telegram preference applies once a channel is linked

auto_follow_assigned.description: Follow the records I am assigned to through a `user` field with `notify_on_assign`. Default `true` (T543, used by T544).

auto_follow_created.description: Follow the records I create by hand (one record at a time; not imports, forms, pastes or automations). Default `true` (T543).

authorization_url.description: Authorization request of the provider (`max_age=0`); open it with a top-level navigation (`window.location.assign`)

last_used_at.description: Written at most once per 5 minutes

user.description: The member who owns the token

next_cursor.description: Cursor for the next page, `null` on the last page

bot_username.description: Username of the bot (`getMe`, without `@`), `null` without bot

delivery_mode.description: `null` without bot; `polling` (default) or `webhook` (Telegram calls Cellhive; needs an `https` `PUBLIC_URL`)

secret_id.description: The `telegram_bot` secret used as notification bot, or `null`

status.description: `null` without bot; `webhook_conflict`: the bot has a webhook elsewhere; `invalid_token`: Telegram refused the token

webhook_available.description: Whether this instance can use the webhook mode: `PUBLIC_URL` is `https` on a port Telegram accepts (443, 80, 88, 8443). `false` → `PATCH { telegram_delivery_mode: webhook }` answers `422` / `PUBLIC_URL_NOT_HTTPS` (T616)

webhook_status.description: `null` unless `delivery_mode` is `webhook`; `error`: Telegram reported a delivery error since the last hourly check, or the webhook no longer points to Cellhive

role.description: The caller's role in the organization

available.description: AI is on: show AI entry points

role.description: The caller's role in the organization

automation_max_depth.description: Automation loop guard (SPEC §11.6): changes made this many automation steps away from a person's change start no run (default 3)

password.description: At least 10 characters, not a common password

revoke_tokens.description: Also revoke every API token of the user, in every organization (default `true`; `false` keeps them working)

headers.description: Headers to send with the `PUT` (`content-type`). The body must be exactly `size` bytes: the signature covers `Content-Length`.

PrincipalType.description: Kind of principal a membership or role is given to

type.description: Problem type URI; ends with the code

code.description: Machine-readable detail code used by the UI for translation

params.description: Parameters for translating the message, e.g. `position`, `limit`

PublicSharingPolicy.description: `allowed` (default), `forms_only` (only form links may be public) or `disabled` (no public link). Public links the policy no longer allows stop working (`410`) but are kept.

branch.description: `true`: also permanently delete the descendants deleted together with each record (sub-records, "delete whole branch") that are in the caller’s trash

confirm_name.description: The table name, typed to confirm (compared exactly after trimming); another value answers `422 VALIDATION_FAILED` / `CONFIRM_NAME_MISMATCH`

ids.description: Ids permanently deleted: the requested ids, then their branches

partner_field_ids.description: Link fields of other tables that pointed at the table: now in the trash and not restorable (`LINK_TABLE_PURGED`)

record_count.description: Records deleted with the table (its trash included)

ReadinessStatus.description: Readiness status: every dependency is up

storage.description: Object storage bucket (or local directory) is reachable

fields.description: Cell values keyed by field name or id. Fields the caller cannot read are absent.

id.description: `null` for an ancestor the caller cannot read (`locked`)

locked.description: The caller cannot read this ancestor: a placeholder without id or title

title.description: Primary field as text; `null` when locked or the primary field is hidden

cells.description: Field id → the first matching cell rule of that field

skip_bulk.description: Ignore bulk changes and imports (ADR-26 §2–3): no run and no circuit-breaker count for them
Ignore bulk changes and imports (ADR-26 §2–3): no run and no circuit-breaker count for them

source.description: What started the follow: `manual` (the follow button), `created` (the caller created the record by hand), `assigned` (the caller was added to a `user` field with `notify_on_assign`). `null` when the caller does not follow the record.

definition.description: The whole new definition. A change makes the caller `run_as` (ADR-25 §2)

version.description: Expected current version (same as `If-Match`); a mismatch is `409`

owner_id.description: Transfers ownership to another member of the organization. Only the current owner or an organization owner/admin.

settings.description: Keys to change (base admins); keys left out keep their value

strict_computed_permissions.description: Formula/lookup values are hidden (`null`, field `locked`) from readers who cannot read a field of the **same** record the value is computed from (SPEC §9.5). Default `false`: like Lark, they see the result. Values computed from other tables are always hidden from readers who cannot read their sources

layout.description: Every widget of the dashboard → its place

name.description: Unique in the base, ignoring case (1–100 characters)

position.description: New index in the base list (clamped)

version.description: Expected current version (same as `If-Match`); a mismatch is `409`

display_name.description: Shown in the `From` header. 1–100 characters; `@`, `<`, `>`, control characters (C0/C1, U+2028/U+2029, bidirectional overrides and isolates) and URL/domain look-alikes (`xxx://`, `www.`, `label.tld`) are refused with `DISPLAY_NAME_NOT_ALLOWED` (`params.reason`: `control_char`, `angle_bracket`, `at_sign`, `url`)

signature_md.description: Narrow Markdown, no placeholders (`{{` → `PLACEHOLDER_NOT_ALLOWED`), at most 2 images `![alt](asset:att_…)` of signature assets of the organization (T534; other image syntax → `IMAGE_SOURCE_NOT_ALLOWED`); added below the body of automation emails sent as the identity (T531)

default_signature_md.description: Narrow Markdown, at most 2000 characters; no placeholders (`{{` → `PLACEHOLDER_NOT_ALLOWED`); at most 2 images `![alt](asset:att_… =width)` of ready signature assets of the organization (`TOO_MANY_IMAGES`, `EMAIL_IMAGE_NOT_FOUND`); any other image syntax (URL, `data:`) → `IMAGE_SOURCE_NOT_ALLOWED`

max_attachment_bytes.description: At most `limits.max_attachment_bytes` (`422 VALIDATION_FAILED` / `TOO_BIG`); `null` = the instance cap

max_attachments.description: At most `limits.max_attachments` (`422 VALIDATION_FAILED` / `TOO_BIG`); `null` = the instance cap

options.description: Top-level keys replace the current ones (e.g. only `style`). For `select`, `options` is the full new list: items with an `id` keep it (rename, recolour, reorder), items without are added, missing ones are deleted and removed from the records by a background job. The column type never changes here (`PUT`). `formula`: `expression` (names) and/or `style`; `lookup`: any of its keys — the definition is checked again like on create (CONTRACTS §13). `datetime`: `reminder` (`DateReminderOption`; `null` turns it off; turning it on or changing it never reminds of moments already passed — CONTRACTS §22.6).

position.description: New 0-based index in the display order (clamped to the last index); the others shift

ai_state.description: Only on AI fields (`options.ai`, T910): counts of rows waiting, failed and paused

button.description: Only on `button` fields returned by the field endpoints (T517): the automation attached to the button and its `min_permission`

automation_id.description: The automation (not deleted) attached to the button; `null` = none

min_permission.description: Least permission on a record to click (`null` without automation)

compute_error.description: Only on `formula`/`lookup` fields: `null`, or the field-level error

refs.description: What the error is about (`REF`: the missing field/table, or the computed field in error it reads; `CIRCLE`: the fields of the cycle; `INVALID_CONFIG`: the converted field, when known). `id`/`name` are `null` for what the reader cannot see: a field or table without read access, a field in the trash without schema rights on its table, a table in the trash for non-admins, anything purged

compute_mode.description: Only on `formula`/`lookup` fields, chosen by the server (SPEC §5.9): `stored` (a column, computed on write) or `virtual` (computed on read: `NOW()`/`TODAY()` or a virtual dependency)

compute_state.description: Only on `formula`/`lookup` fields: `ready`, `backfilling` (values being computed for every record), `recomputing` (a write changed more than 1 000 rows of it, or every row: the `computed.recompute` job catches up and rows not recomputed yet keep their previous values) or `error` (see `compute_error`)

deleted_at.description: Only on fields in the trash, listed with `include_deleted=true`: when the field was deleted (restorable for 30 days)

job_id.description: The `schema.remove_select_options` job queued because select options were deleted, or the `computed.backfill` job of a changed stored formula/lookup (follow it with `GET /jobs/:id` or `job.progress` on `user:{id}`); `null` when the change queued no such job

link_table_purged.description: Only on `link` fields in the trash (listed with `include_deleted=true`) whose linked table was purged (`true`, T461): the links are gone and a restore answers `422 VALIDATION_FAILED` / `LINK_TABLE_PURGED` (CONTRACTS §13)

link_target_deleted.description: Only on `link` fields whose linked table is in the trash (`true`): the field stays, its cells read empty and take no new links until the table is restored (CONTRACTS §13)

locked.description: Only on `formula`/`lookup` fields (T457): `true` when the reader cannot read what the value is computed from — another table, a field of other records, or (base setting `strict_computed_permissions`) a field of the same record it cannot read. Its cells read `null`; filtering, sorting and grouping by it answer like a hidden field (`422 INVALID_FILTER` / `INVALID_SORT`). Also on AI fields (T910, always strict): `true` when the reader cannot read every field of its prompt

result_type.description: Only on `formula`/`lookup` fields: the type of their value (T456)

apiToken.description: Personal API token (`Authorization: Bearer cht_…`, CONTRACTS §26). The header wins over the session cookie (never read then) and needs no CSRF token. An operation accepts a token only when its `security` lists `apiToken` with the scope it needs (`x-api-token-scope`; `*:write` never implies `*:read`); other routes answer `403 INSUFFICIENT_SCOPE` (`errors[0].params.required`: the scope, or `["session"]`). The token acts as its user's current access, limited to its organization and `base_ids` (anything outside → `404`). Malformed, unknown, revoked (`TOKEN_REVOKED`), expired (`TOKEN_EXPIRED`) or disabled tokens → `401` with `WWW-Authenticate: Bearer error="invalid_token"`. Rate limits: 60 requests/s per token, 20 requests/s per token and base (`429 RATE_LIMITED` + `Retry-After`).

sessionCookie.description: Session cookie set by `POST /api/v1/auth/login`. Requests other than GET/HEAD/OPTIONS that carry the session cookie must send the value of the `ob_csrf` cookie in the `x-csrf-token` header, otherwise `403 CSRF_INVALID`.

delete.description: Session only: an API token can never manage tokens. The owner, or an owner/admin of its organization; anyone else gets `404`. The token stops authenticating at once (`401 TOKEN_REVOKED`) and its WebSocket connections close; it stays listed 90 days. Revoking again changes nothing. Audited as `api_token.revoked`. Requires the `x-csrf-token` header (value of the `ob_csrf` cookie) when authenticated by the session cookie.

get.description: Public; reached through the provider's redirect. The `ob_oidc` cookie is cleared first (one use) and `state` compared in constant time; the code is exchanged (PKCE, `client_secret_basic`) and the ID token checked (issuer, audience, `azp`, expiry, `iat`, `nonce`, JWKS signature). The identity is `(provider, sub)`; an unknown one creates an account only when the provider allows sign-up, the email is verified and its domain allowed (§27.2). Success: new session (`ob_session` + `ob_csrf`, a previous session is revoked) and redirect to `next`. A user with the same email is linked only when the provider sets `LINK_BY_EMAIL=true` and `email_verified` is the JSON boolean `true`, else `OIDC_ACCOUNT_EXISTS`. Failures redirect to `/login?error=<CODE>` (CONTRACTS §27.2: `OIDC_STATE_INVALID`, `OIDC_PROVIDER_ERROR`, `OIDC_ACCOUNT_EXISTS`, `OIDC_SIGNUP_DISABLED`, `OIDC_EMAIL_UNVERIFIED`, `OIDC_DOMAIN_NOT_ALLOWED`, `UNAUTHENTICATED` for a disabled account, `RATE_LIMITED`), never a problem document. An attempt started by `POST /me/identities/{provider}/start` links the identity to the signed-in user instead (no new session) and redirects to `/account/connections`; Failures redirect to `/account/connections?error=<CODE>` (CONTRACTS §27.3: `OIDC_STATE_INVALID` — also when the session changed since `start` —, `OIDC_PROVIDER_ERROR` — also an ID token without a recent `auth_time` —, `IDENTITY_IN_USE`).

post.description: Run history is for people who manage the automation (ADR-25 §3); anyone else — also someone who sees the automation but cannot manage it — gets `404` (runs carry record data). A `queued` or `waiting` run becomes `cancelled` (`error.code = cancelled_by_user`); its waiting steps too. Audited as `automation.run.cancelled`. With an `Idempotency-Key` header the response is stored for 24 hours per user: sending the same key again returns the stored response (header `Idempotent-Replayed: true`); the same key with another request, or while the first request is still running, is `409 IDEMPOTENCY_KEY_REUSED`. Failed requests are not stored; a request that left its key in progress for more than 60 seconds is considered dead and the key can be reused. Requires the `x-csrf-token` header (value of the `ob_csrf` cookie) when authenticated by the session cookie.

Creates a new `queued` run with the automation's **current** definition and version and the original trigger (`rerun_of`, `rerun_by`). With an `Idempotency-Key` header the response is stored for 24 hours per user: sending the same key again returns the stored response (header `Idempotent-Replayed: true`); the same key with another request, or while the first request is still running, is `409 IDEMPOTENCY_KEY_REUSED`. post.description: Session only, with the CSRF header (`X-CSRF-Token`); a `POST` so that another site cannot start a link with the caller's session. Sets the state cookie in `link` mode (`ob_oidc`, `Path=/api/v1/auth/oidc/`, bound to the caller and the current session) and returns the authorization URL, which the web client opens with a top-level navigation. The request carries `max_age=0` (the provider authenticates the person again) and the callback requires an ID token `auth_time` at most 10 minutes old. The provider redirects to the same `…/callback`, which attaches `(provider, sub)` to the caller: the identity of another user, or another account of the same provider already connected → `IDENTITY_IN_USE`; the same account again → its email is refreshed. Audited as `auth.identity_linked` (one entry per organization of the user). Shares the 20 per minute per IP limit of sign-in; ignores `Idempotency-Key`. Failures redirect to `/account/connections?error=<CODE>` (CONTRACTS §27.3: `OIDC_STATE_INVALID` — also when the session changed since `start` —, `OIDC_PROVIDER_ERROR` — also an ID token without a recent `auth_time` —, `IDENTITY_IN_USE`).

The value is sealed with AES-256-GCM and never returned, logged or audited — except a `webhook_signing` value the server generated (`generate: true`), returned once in `value`. `http_header` / `webhook_signing` / `ai_api_key` need `allowed_hosts`: automations (the AI provider for `ai_api_key`, T906) send them only to those hosts (T701). Audited as `secret.created` (name, kind, scope, allowed hosts). With an `Idempotency-Key` header the response is stored for 24 hours per user: sending the same key again returns the stored response (header `Idempotent-Replayed: true`); the same key with another request, or while the first request is still running, is `409 IDEMPOTENCY_KEY_REUSED`. Failed requests are not stored; a request that left its key in progress for more than 60 seconds is considered dead and the key can be reused. Requires the `x-csrf-token` header (value of the `ob_csrf` cookie) when authenticated by the session cookie.

Every response carries `X-Robots-Tag: noindex, nofollow`, `Referrer-Policy: no-referrer` and `Cache-Control: no-store`. Dashboard links only (T809): a view or form link, or a widget of another dashboard, is `404`. Widgets in reading order; one the link cannot read is `status = no_permission`, one naming a deleted table or field `broken` — both without `config`. A `config` never carries the saved `filter` (always `null`; still applied by the server). Global filters keep only targets the link reads; `fields` lists the fields the configuration names, with display options only (as `meta`). `settings.allow_export` is the link setting and the creator’s current `base_rule.download`. No realtime: the page polls the widgets every `settings.refresh_seconds`. Counts one access of the link.

post.description: Acts with the link’s access (its creator’s current access ∩ the form fields, create only). Audience `org` needs a signed-in member of the organization (`401`; other users `404`); `require_login` needs any signed-in user (`401`). Signed-in submitters of such links are the actor and `created_by`; other submissions are anonymous (actor `share_link`, `created_by` `null`); all carry `via.share_link_id`. Needs `submit_token` (`422 SUBMIT_TOKEN_INVALID` / `SUBMITTED_TOO_FAST`); a non-empty `honeypot` gets the normal response and writes nothing. `user` questions are answered only through `org` links, with members who can open the base (`422 INVALID_CELL_VALUE` / `USER_NOT_FOUND` otherwise), `link` questions only through `org` links with records the creator reads that match `record_filter` (`422 LINK_TARGET_NOT_FOUND` otherwise); a `public` link treats both as fields outside the form (`422 VALIDATION_FAILED` / `UNKNOWN_FIELD`). Attachment answers are files uploaded with the same `submit_token` through `POST /shares/{token}/uploads` (else `422 INVALID_CELL_VALUE` / `ATTACHMENT_NOT_FOUND`). 10 submissions/minute per client IP (`429`). No `Idempotency-Key`. One record per submission, created like `POST /tables/{id}/records?typecast=true&field_key_type=id` (base locale; select options are never created). Only fields of the form (`422 VALIDATION_FAILED` / `UNKNOWN_FIELD` at `fields.<id>`); fields the form requires (on top of the table) need a non-empty value (`422 REQUIRED_FIELD_MISSING`). Value errors (`INVALID_CELL_VALUE`, `INVALID_SELECT_OPTION`, …) have paths `fields.<id>`. Emits `record.created` and `form.submitted` with their audit entries in one transaction. Requires the `x-csrf-token` header (value of the `ob_csrf` cookie) when authenticated by the session cookie.

The model sees only the fields the caller reads (names, types, option names — never values or ids) and answers with a plan by name; the server turns it into a temporary widget checked like a saved one (errors go back to the model, at most 2 repair rounds) and computes it like `POST /widgets/{widgetId}/data` with the caller's permissions. `unanswerable` when the question needs a field the caller cannot read or that does not exist (never says which). A narrative only when the organization lets AI see record data (a second call with the aggregated rows). Nothing is stored or cached. Counts towards the quota (feature `ask`) and the AI rate limit; audited as `ai.requested` (CONTRACTS §29.4). Requires the `x-csrf-token` header (value of the `ob_csrf` cookie) when authenticated by the session cookie.
